TX.grade_reason: Bulk, free, no login. The nightly Drilling Permit Master and Trailer file has one record per permit and amendment with the issue (approval) date, received date, application type, depth, county, district, operator number and spud date; the monthly and End of Month files give the history. The tracker already builds monthly and daily permit counts from it.
TX.producer_plan: Already built (d1 monthly, d7 daily). Monthly: read the Drilling Permit Master and Trailer (daf802), keep record 02 per permit number, count by issue month; new drill is application type 01 (first record per permit number with a valid issue date). Other bands by the same type code: 07 re-enter, 14 recomplete, 15 reclass, 09 field transfer; amendments are the records with a sequence number below 99 or an amended date. Injection and disposal appear only as W-1s whose field well code is I or D (record 03); permits for injection wells on other UIC forms were not examined. Daily: the plain daf420.dat (current month, lags one business day) plus month-end files for earlier months, and the twice-daily pending sets for the queue. Caveats: the permit file stores an internal district code; coordinates in the file cover only part of recent permits (4 to 39 percent in several months of 2026), so counts never come from the dots (the RRC map layer fills them in); the dated snapshots turn to a new month on the 3rd; a file holds one month plus earlier permits touched that month.
TX.privacy: The permit files hold operator names and numbers (some operators are individuals, so the tracker names only P-5 corporations, LLCs and limited partnerships), an alternate-address record, and in the pending set the operator's mailing address and phone columns. The W-1 certificate asks for a representative's name, phone and optional e-mail; W-1 letters and plats and completion attachments can carry…

NM.grade_reason: The public well layer is bulk, free and reachable, with one record per well, but it has no approval date: it counts wells by spud date (reported about two months late) and has no work type. Approval dates exist only as effective_date on the MapServer copy for wells still in status New, so they fade for older months. The tracker counts wells spudded; the OCD publishes no approvals by well and date.
NM.producer_plan: Monthly counts as the tracker builds them: read the Wells_Public layer with paged ?f=json queries (id, type, status, ogrid, ogrid_name, county_code, latitude, longitude, spud_date), count one well per API number on its spud day, drop the placeholder years 9999 and 1900, and show a month only after a 60-day lag. Activity bands: wells are all new wells; injection and disposal wells separate by the type field; no re-entry, recompletion or amendment is visible. Approval counts: query the MapServer layer for status = New and effective_date in the day or month (exact for recent weeks only), and keep each night's count so that older months stop depending on wells that leave status New. The layer's historic-moment archive gives additions per month but not which wells.
NM.privacy: The layer holds operator names and OGRIDs, well names, API numbers and surface coordinates; no contact details were in its schema. An OGRID name can be an individual, so the tracker names only corporations, LLCs and partnerships. The C-101 and the scanned well files carry signers' names, e-mail addresses and phone numbers (none copied here).

FO.grade_reason: The weekly borehole file is bulk, free and reachable, with one row per borehole, but it has spud dates and no approval date or permit type, so counts measure wells spudded. Approval dates, received dates and permit types (new well, sidetrack, bypass, revised) are published only in the online APD query, a grid with CSV export that was not scripted here.
FO.producer_plan: As the tracker does: read the weekly borehole zip (no header; 29 fields), take the first ten digits of the API number as the well, count it on the spud day of its earliest borehole (field 5), place it by surface area and block (field 11), name the operator from the company file by operator number (field 3), and show a month only after a 60-day lag. Unzip into its own folder, read the dBASE file with the standard library (record length 1,025; PermitDate is YYYYMMDD, 00000000 means missing), and count rows by month of PermitDate, dropping future or zero dates. Split by the type code: OIL and GAS as new drill, SWD, EOR and BDW as injection or disposal, GSR, GSC and MON as storage or monitor, ST and CORE as test wells; note the type is the well's current type, so a recent permit later logged as a dry hole (DH) changes band, and months must be recounted each run. Re-entries, workovers, conversions and operator changes are not separate in the bulk files: they would need the Permit Search report (permit type column), which the page builds by script, so test it by hand before relying on it. VA.grade_reason: The ArcGIS well layers are free, no login and answered from here, one record per well, but they hold only a status date (FiStatDt), a drilling-complete date and a well-completion date, not a labeled permit issue date, and a well leaves the 'undrilled' layer once drilled. Counts of wells completed per month are possible; permits issued per month are not from the layers. The 'Permit Issuance' reports in the DGO Inquiry may give issue dates but are postback pages (unread). Virginia is almost all coalbed methane and gas.
VA.producer_plan: Option 1, history: query layer 0 (Active Wells) in pages of 2000 and count FiDrComp (drilling complete) and FiWellComp (well completion) by month, split by TblOpDesc; this measures wells drilled or completed, like New Mexico's spuds, with a lag. Option 2, permits going forward: query layer 4 (Permitted Undrilled Wells) and layer 1 (Pending Wells) every night and keep a log of each FiNo with its TblPsDesc and FiStatDt; the first night a FiNo appears with TblPsDesc 'Issued' and its FiStatDt gives an approximate issue month, and Pending Wells gives applications waiting. Wells leave layer 4 when drilled, so history cannot be rebuilt from it. Check whether FiStatDt on an 'Issued' row is the issue date (many fall on the same day in pairs and threes, which looks like batches, but this is not confirmed). Option 3: the DGO Inquiry 'Permit Issuance' and 'Permit Issuance Statistics' reports, if they give issue dates; they need an ASP.NET form post, which is fragile. The VGOB service is not started. Work type is not a field (new vs modification is separate layers: Pending Wells vs Pending Well Modifications).
VA.privacy: Layers hold company names (CoName) and farm names (FiFarm, often a landowner's family name); no phone or street address seen in the field list. A build needs a corporate-name filter on operators and should not publish farm names. The form collects owner addresses (not read).
